# License and documents

This page is for developers and designers who publish a site package, and for reviewers who check one. A package
that does not say under which license it is published gives nobody the right to use, change or pass it on. This
page explains the two places a package states its license, how Exponential shows them, and what the shipped
packages do. It is not legal advice; for choosing a license see
[Licensing choices: an overview](../../designers/distribution/licensing-choices-overview.md).

## Two places, both conventions

| Where | Form | Enforced |
|---|---|---|
| `<licence>` in `package.xml` | An identifier, such as `GPL-2.0-or-later` | Only by the package creation wizards, which offer a strict choice. An import accepts any text or none |
| `documents/LICENCE` in the archive, named in `<documents>` | A plain text file | No. The package page links it when it is there |

Both spellings, `<licence>` and `LICENCE`, are the literal names the package format uses and stay as they are.
Every package published on the package server is expected to carry both; reviewers check for them
([Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md)).

## The licence element

`eZPackage::parseDOMTree()` reads the text of the first `<licence>` element and keeps it as it is. When the kernel
writes a package (`eZPackage::domStructure()`), `<licence>` follows the `<version>` and the release `<timestamp>`:

```xml
<version>
  <number>6.0</number>
  <release>15-stable</release>
</version>
<licence>GPL-2.0-or-later</licence>
<state>stable</state>
```

The creation wizards (`kernel/classes/ezpackagecreationhandler.php`) refuse a license that is not in
`[LicenseSettings] LicenseList[]` of `settings/package.ini` ("choose one from the list") and store the identifier.
A package written by hand should use the same identifiers: an SPDX identifier where one exists
([spdx.org/licenses](https://spdx.org/licenses/)), otherwise `LicenseRef-<name>`.

## How a stored license is shown

The package page (`package/view/full/<name>`) shows the license through `eZPackageLicense::describe()` in
`kernel/classes/ezpackagelicense.php`:

| Stored value | Shown as |
|---|---|
| An identifier of `LicenseList[]`, such as `GPL-2.0-or-later` | The license's `Name=` as a link to its `URL=`, followed by the identifier |
| An alias of `[LicenseSettings] AliasList[]`, such as `GPL` | The license it stands for, plus "stored as GPL" |
| Any other text | The text as it is, without a link |
| Nothing | A dash |

The shipped settings define 46 licenses in nine groups, `DefaultLicense=GPL-2.0-or-later`, and one alias:

```ini
[LicenseSettings]
AliasList[]
AliasList[GPL]=GPL-2.0-or-later
```

The comment above it explains why: packages made before the license became a choice store `GPL`, which always
meant the GNU GPL version 2 or (at your option) any later version, the license of Exponential itself. Adding your
own license to the list is described in
[Package licenses and Semantic Versioning](../../../features/6.0/package-licenses-and-versions.md).

## The documents element and documents/LICENCE

Documents are files for the reader of a package, kept in the `documents/` directory of the package
(`eZPackage::documentDirectory()`). `package.xml` names each one:

```xml
<documents>
  <document mime-type="text/plain" name="LICENCE" />
</documents>
```

| Attribute | Read | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | The file name below `documents/` |
| `mime-type` | yes | `text/plain` when the writer is given none |
| `os`, `audience` | yes | Optional; the shipped packages leave them out |

What happens to a document:

- **Export** keeps it: `eZPackage::exportToArchive()` copies `documents/`, `files/`, `simplefiles/`, `settings/`
  and the sub-directories of the install items, and nothing else.
- **The package page** lists the documents under Details. Each one that is in the archive opens in the page's
  contents browser (issue #389); a link straight to the file under `var/storage` is refused by the web server.
- **Nothing refuses** a package without documents, or one that names a document it does not carry.

> **Note**
> Before 6.0.15 a file at the top of the package that was not in one of the exported directories was lost when the
> package was exported again from the administration. From 6.0.15 on the export takes every file and folder at the
> top (`eZPackage::extraTopLevelEntries()`; not hidden ones, not symbolic links). Keep `LICENCE` in `documents/`
> anyway: that is where the package page lists documents.

## What the shipped packages carry

Checked in the two source repositories on 2026-10-18:

- All 16 packages have `<licence>GPL</licence>`, shown as "GNU General Public License v2.0 or later (stored as GPL)".
- All 16 have `documents/LICENCE`, a 15-line GPL notice ("version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later
  version"), named in `<documents>`.
- The first line of each names the package ("This file is part of the package ..."). Until 2026-10-19 three of
  them named another package, a leftover of copying: `sevenx_multisite_clean` named `sevenx_multisite`, and both
  `sevenx_multisite_democontent` packages named `sevenx_democontent`. Fixed in the source repository on 2026-10-19,
  and the rebuilt packages are on the package server.
- Both source repositories have a `LICENSE` file with the full text of the GNU GPL version 2 since 2026-10-19.

> **Tip**
> When you fork a package, change the first line of `documents/LICENCE` to the new package name, and add your own
> copyright line if your changes are substantial
> ([Copyright and author lines](../../designers/extensions/copyright-and-author-lines.md)).

## Checklist

- [ ] `<licence>` holds an identifier from `[LicenseSettings] LicenseList[]` (or `GPL`, the alias the shipped
      packages use).
- [ ] `documents/LICENCE` exists and states the same license.
- [ ] `<documents>` names it with `mime-type="text/plain"`.
- [ ] The first line of `LICENCE` names this package.
- [ ] Images, fonts or scripts under other terms are named with their license in the source repository's README
      ([README and repository docs](readme-and-repository-docs.md)).
